about: What cfml-m1.1 ported into crates/calc-fml/src/syntax from the pinned OxFml syntax sources, what it changed and why, what it left out with the beads that will need it (found by the search it records), and each OxFml test of that syntax whose expectation the port keeps, changes or drops. Only this bead writes this file.

sources.pin: migration/source-manifest.json (pin date 2026-10-15); the blob equals the pin's

kept: every character lands in exactly one token and one Eof token ends the list
operator tokens, with <=, <> and >= as two-character tokens
error literals tried in the same order, matched without regard to ASCII case
string literals and quoted names with a doubled quote as an escaped quote; unterminated quoted text runs to the end of the input
bracket groups with ' escaping #, [, ], @ and ', followed by identifier-continue characters, as one BracketedQualifier
number literals: digits, an optional fraction, an exponent only when digits follow it; a '.' before a digit starts a number (except right after ':', see the changes)

identifier start (any letter, _, $, \) and continue (letters, digits, combining marks, ., _, $) rules, embedded bracket groups, and the break before '.' followed by '@', '*' or '[' (and now ':', see the changes)
runs of ASCII whitespace as one Whitespace token; any other character as one Unknown token

changes.change: Spans are UTF-16 code units of the input. The pinned lexer used char indices for tokens and the UTF-8 byte length for the Eof span, so the two disagreed for non-ASCII input.
changes.reason: The bead asks for UTF-16 editor offsets. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip (the UTF-16 slices of every token and trivia tile the input; '&' after the string "\u{1F600}x" starts at 6).

changes.change: The error-literal spellings live in token.rs ERROR_LITERALS, each paired with its calc-value WorksheetErrorCode; Token::error_code maps a literal to its code.
changes.reason: The tree names the worksheet error a literal spells through the prerequisite value API (cfunc-m0.1). Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip (all fourteen codes, upper and lower case).

changes.change: is_identifier_letter and is_identifier_word_char are folded into the private is_identifier_start and is_identifier_continue.
changes.reason: Their other users (the language service's completion scanners and the editor's name renderer) are not ported; see not_ported.

changes.change: An identifier ends before a '.' followed by ':', a number literal stops before a '.' followed by ':', and a '.' right after ':' is a Dot token even before a digit. The pinned lexer read 'A1.' in 'A1.:B10' as one identifier, '1.' in '1.:3' as one number and '.3' in '1:.3' as one number, so those trim references parsed as ranges with no diagnostic.
changes.reason: Trim references ('A1.:B10', 'A1:.B10', 'A1.:.B10') are Excel syntax this bead does not parse; the lexer exposes the trim operator so the parser can refuse it (see the parser.rs changes). Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip (the three A1 forms) and the calc-fml unit test trim_references_are_refused_as_unsupported_syntax (also 'A:.A', '1:.3', '1.:3' and 'Sheet1!A1.:B10'); with the identifier break removed, both fail.

changes.change: trailing_trivia is removed: whitespace is the leading trivia of the next token only, and whitespace after the last token is the leading trivia of the Eof token.
changes.reason: The pinned attach pass gave the whitespace between two tokens to both (trailing of the first, leading of the second), so a reprint had to pick one. Each piece of whitespace now appears once and the tree reprints by concatenation. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip.

changes.change: A missing token has missing = true and an empty span at the insertion point (right after the last token taken). The pinned parser gave an expected-but-absent token empty text and the current token's span.
changes.reason: Spans then never decrease in tree order and never cover text the token does not hold. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip ('=SUM(A1,' has its missing ')' at 8).

changes.change: Fields are private with accessors; new and the trivia setter are crate-private; with_trivia is removed.
changes.reason: Only the lexer and parser build tokens, which keeps the lossless invariant.

changes.change: error_code() is added.
changes.reason: See the lexer.rs changes.

kept: text and span

changes.change: SyntaxTriviaKind (Whitespace, Unknown) is dropped; trivia is whitespace.
changes.reason: Only Whitespace is trivia (TokenKind::is_trivia), so Unknown trivia was never produced.

kept: message, span and kind
Message and SpacedRangeColon { suggested }

changes.reason: The bead refuses selector syntax at entry with a precise unsupported-syntax diagnostic. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__tree_syntax_rejected.

changes.change: SpaceBeforeCall is not ported; the Default derive and the public constructor new give way to the crate-private constructors message and unsupported.
changes.reason: SpaceBeforeCall needs the function catalogue (see not_ported); only the parser makes diagnostics.

sources.pin: migration/source-manifest.json (pin date 2026-10-15); the blob equals the pin's

kept: an optional leading '='; trailing tokens kept with one diagnostic each
the precedence chain comparison, &, + -, * /, ^, postfix %, prefix + -, union, intersection, range, postfix # and invocation
the union comma only where commas separate nothing else (not in argument lists or array literals)
intersection as whitespace before the start of a reference; a range colon must follow its left operand immediately
the sheet-span lookahead ': Identifier !' (a quoted first sheet allowed, a quoted last sheet not)
qualified references, calls by name, invocation of any expression, grouping, array literals with ',' and ';', argument lists with omitted arguments
the spaced-range-colon recovery: a RangeExpr, one SpacedRangeColon diagnostic and a suggestion without the recovered whitespace

changes.change: The input is the formula text (parse_formula(&str) -> SyntaxTree), not a ParseRequest over a FormulaSourceRecord; the worksheet-cell-entry literal path is not ported.
changes.reason: See not_ported.

changes.change: The selector productions are gone. A '^' run (with an optional '.name') where an operand starts, a '.' selector where an operand starts, and a '.' member selector after an operand each become one UnsupportedExpr with one UnsupportedSyntax diagnostic spanning exactly the selector tokens. The pinned parser built HostReferenceCollectionExpr nodes (with synthetic SELF and PARENT tokens) and HostMemberReferenceExpr nodes, or, for a leading '.' with no selector syntax configured, an untyped diagnostic and a MissingExpr holding only the '.'.
changes.reason: The bead: remove the selector grammar at entry, not as a later rejection. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__tree_syntax_rejected, which also checks that neighbouring Excel forms (2^3, 2^-1, @A1:A3, @Parent.Value, Base.Value, .5+1, Sheet1!A1#) parse without a diagnostic.

changes.change: '@' always prefixes a full range operand. The pinned parser special-cased '@' before an identifier or '*': '@SEQUENCE(3)' became InvokeExpr(IdentifierExpr) instead of a call, '@*' became an IdentifierExpr over '*', and '@Sheet1!A1' left '!A1' unparsed.
changes.reason: Those branches served selector syntax; without it '@' is Excel's implicit-intersection prefix. pb_004 ('=@A1#' is a PrefixExpr) is kept, and '=@A1:A3' is asserted in both test suites.

changes.change: An error literal parses as ErrorLiteralExpr, except '#REF!' (in any ASCII case) directly followed by an identifier or a number: that is a QualifiedReferenceExpr whose qualifier is the '#REF!' token, which holds the '!', and whose target is the reference, the form Excel writes after the referenced sheet is deleted. The pinned parser put every error literal in an IdentifierExpr, so '=#REF!A1' ended with a trailing-token diagnostic and '=SUM(#REF!A1:B2)' with a missing ')' and trailing tokens.
changes.reason: Real Excel files contain '#REF!A1' and '#REF!A1:B2'; refusing them would refuse those files' formulas. Evaluating the reference to #REF! belongs to binding and evaluation (cfml-m1.2, cfml-m1.3). Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip ('=#REF!A1', '=SUM(#REF!A1:B2)', and the qualifier token's error code) and the calc-fml unit test deleted_sheet_ref_qualifies_a_reference ('=#ref!$B$2', '=SUM(#REF!1:3)'; '=#REF!', '=Sheet2!#REF!' and '=SUM(#REF!,A1)' stay error literals; '=#DIV/0!A1' does not qualify); with the qualifier rule changed to '#NAME?', both fail.

changes.change: Intersections chain inside argument lists and array literals. The pinned parse_intersection returned after the first intersection when the union comma was disallowed, so '=SUM(A1:C3 B1:B5 A2:C2)' got a missing-')' diagnostic and trailing-token diagnostics, while the same operands chained at the top level. The early return dates from OxFml's bootstrap commit 0371210, which states no reason.
changes.reason: One operand grammar wherever an operand appears. No Excel capture witnesses the three-operand form in this bead; the parser's behaviour is witnessed by the calc-fml unit test intersections_chain_inside_an_argument_list.

changes.change: Whitespace becomes leading trivia as the parser takes tokens; whitespace that does not turn out to be an intersection is given back by resetting the position. The pinned parser dropped skipped whitespace and re-attached it in a pass over the finished tree (attach_trivia_to_green_tree, rehydrate_green_node_tokens).
changes.reason: Each piece of whitespace is owned and reprinted once.

changes.change: At the end of input an expected operand is an empty MissingExpr with the diagnostic 'expected an expression' at the insertion point. The pinned parser reported 'unexpected token Eof' and put a clone of the Eof token in the MissingExpr, so Eof appeared twice in the tree.
changes.reason: Lossless reprint of incomplete input. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip ('=', '', '=(1+', '=Sheet1!').

changes.change: Unterminated string literals and quoted names get a diagnostic ('unterminated string literal', 'unterminated quoted name') at the token's span; the pinned parser accepted them with no diagnostic.
changes.reason: Incomplete input must not parse as a well-formed formula. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip ('="abc', '="abc""', "='My Sheet").

changes.change: The space-before-call recovery is not ported, so '=SUM (A1)' parses as the intersection of the name SUM and (A1) with no diagnostic (pinned: a CallExpr with one SpaceBeforeCall diagnostic).
changes.reason: It consults the function catalogue (semantics::lookup_function_meta over OxFunc), which calc-fml does not have yet; see not_ported. Witnessed by the calc-fml unit test space_before_call_is_an_intersection_without_the_catalogue.

changes.change: The operand after a qualifier's '!' (a sheet qualifier, a sheet span or '#REF!') never starts a sheet span. The pinned parser let it, so '=SUM(Sheet1!A1:Sheet1!B2)' and '=SUM(Sheet1!A:Sheet1!C)' parsed as QualifiedReferenceExpr(Sheet1 ! SheetSpan3DReferenceExpr(A1 : Sheet1 ! B2)), the cell A1 read as a first sheet, with no diagnostic. They are now RangeExpr(QualifiedReferenceExpr, QualifiedReferenceExpr).
changes.reason: A1 references with a sheet qualifier are in the bead's Do. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip (both forms and "'Annual Data'!A:'Annual Data'!C") and the calc-fml unit test qualified_range_ends_are_two_qualified_references; with the rule removed, both fail. The quoted forms of sheet_span_3d_reference_tests.rs keep their expectations (sheet_spans_claim_their_colon_only_before_a_bang).

changes.change: A trim operator ('.:', ':.' or '.:.', with no whitespace inside it) after a range operand becomes an UnsupportedExpr over the left operand, the operator tokens and the right operand, with one UnsupportedSyntax diagnostic that names trim references and spans exactly the operator tokens. The pinned parser built a RangeExpr over the name 'A1.' for 'A1.:B10' and over the numbers '1.' and '.3' for '1.:3' and '1:.3', and gave 'A1:.B10' an untyped 'unexpected token Dot' diagnostic followed by further untyped diagnostics.
changes.reason: Excel reads these as trim references, which this bead does not parse: the parser refuses them precisely instead of building a wrong range. dc-2oc4 owns parsing and evaluating them. Witnessed by cfml_m1_1__lossless_roundtrip and trim_references_are_refused_as_unsupported_syntax; with the parser's trim check disabled, both fail.

owner_search.rule: The beads of each not_ported entry are the beads the pin lists for the six syntax inputs (cfml-m1.1, cfml-m2.5, cfml-m6.2) whose Do names the item's job, plus the beads docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md matches for its terms, found with grep -n -i -E "incremental|host-reference|host reference|input pars|cell input|typed constant|entered|template id|canonical token|function/name diagnostics|editor reference|completion" docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md and grep -n -i -E "CellInput|localized input|input text|typed value|cell entry|entry pars|numeric parsing" docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md.
owner_search.inputs: The pinned inputs assigned to cfml-m1.1 are the entries of migration/source-manifest.json whose beads include cfml-m1.1: 65 in all, 6 syntax sources (ported), 4 other sources (not ported), 26 test files and test helpers, and 29 fixtures. Each was looked up with cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup; the exits and calls_quarantined lists in this record come from those transcripts.
owner_search.legacy_tests: Test names are the #[test] functions of each pinned blob (git show 15daac56:<path> in OxFml). Owners are the CalcFml beads whose Do in docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md names the test's subject, read bead by bead (cfml-m1.2 to cfml-m6.2), plus cfunc-m3.17 and onecalc-m2.1 found by name. Subjects no CalcFml Do names were searched, case-insensitively, in the text of every bead of BEAD_DETAILS.md: 'replay bundle|witness bundle|pack candidate|replay adapter|replay fixture' matched only ceng-m4.6, whose capture/replay adapter supplies external and RTD values, not OxFml's replay formats; 'managed session|formula token' and 'scheduler contract' matched nothing; 'reference profile|bind profile|ReferenceBindProfile|host-reference|host reference' matched only cfml-m1.1's removal of host-reference syntax and the Port-from lines that say to discard the tree profile. Those subjects therefore list no bead.

limits: What this record says the pinned parser did comes from reading the pinned blobs; the OxFml tests were not run by this bead (the legacy repositories are read-only inputs).

No Excel capture is consulted by this bead. The grammar's agreement with Excel rests on the ported OxFml rules and their recorded expectations; the one grammar change made without the pin's backing is the intersection chain inside argument lists (see the parser.rs changes).
That Excel writes '#REF!A1' after a sheet is deleted and reads 'A1.:B10' as a trim reference comes from the round-1 review of this bead (2026-10-19), not from an Excel capture made by this bead.
'=SUM (A1)' parses without a diagnostic, as an intersection, until the function catalogue reaches the parser (cfml-m2.5).

Unbalanced brackets in a bracketed qualifier or a structured-reference identifier ('=[abc', '=Table1[Col') are not diagnosed at parse time; structured and external references are bound by cfml-m3.2 and cfml-m3.5.

Trim references ('A1.:B10', 'A1:.B10', 'A1.:.B10', and the same operators between rows, columns or a qualified reference) are refused with one UnsupportedSyntax diagnostic and an UnsupportedExpr, not parsed into a reference; dc-2oc4 owns parsing and evaluating them. A trim operator after whitespace ('=SUM(A1 :.B10)') is not named as one: the formula is refused with a SpacedRangeColon diagnostic, an 'unexpected token Dot' diagnostic and further untyped diagnostics, and no UnsupportedSyntax diagnostic (asserted by trim_references_are_refused_as_unsupported_syntax).
calc-fml's seams.json names callers inside calc-fml only (the lexer and parser functions); whether the registered case reaches each caller is unproven until dc-pz3u.
